claim: Scopus's Content Selection and Advisory Board (CSAB) continually re-evaluates already-indexed journals and can discontinue coverage if they become predatory or decline in quality.
stance_target: students must actively verify current Scopus indexing status, not rely on a journal's past reputation
quoted_support: Scopus is curated by a Content Selection and Advisory Board (CSAB)... these experts determine whether journals are eligible for indexing in Scopus, and they continually re-evaluate these titles to make sure quality is maintained.

claim: There is no universally agreed-upon definition of a predatory journal; predatory behavior exists on a spectrum and can develop over time in a previously legitimate title.
stance_target: predatory-journal risk is not a one-time check but requires ongoing verification even for previously-indexed venues
quoted_support: There is no universally agreed upon definition of a predatory journal or publisher... a journal can become predatory over time.

claim: The Nature/Scientometrics research on predatory journals being indexed in Scopus, which this Elsevier article responds to, was itself retracted on September 6, 2021.
quoted_support: The research referred to here on alleged predatory journals being indexed in Scopus was retracted on September 6, 2021.
